exercises.title: SPI 1 — which fundamental of process improvement?
exercises.problemHtml:
Four SPI fundamentals: (1) improvement is evolutionary and continuous — start small, adjust, pick low-hanging fruit; (2) people change only with an incentive — the strongest is pain from previous projects; (3) improvement is goal-oriented; (4) treat improvement activities as mini-projects with plans and resources. Which fundamental does each statement apply?

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: SPI 2 — root cause analysis
exercises.problemHtml:
Do root cause analysis before changing practices: distinguish symptoms from causes by asking "why?" several times. A cause-and-effect (fishbone, Ishikawa) diagram shows the answers as bones; the most highly branched bones reveal fundamental causes. You need not tackle every cause — a Pareto analysis focuses on the few causes behind most problems.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: SPI 3 — a Pareto analysis
exercises.problemHtml:
The project’s rework hours were tagged with their causes (CAUSES). Write function pareto(counts, threshold) that returns the causes, highest first (ties by name), taken until their cumulative share of the total reaches at least threshold percent — the "vital few" to fix first. Return [] for an empty object.

Requirements

  • pareto(CAUSES, 80) ⇒ the first three causes (81%).
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Viết pareto(counts, threshold): lấy nguyên nhân theo thứ tự giảm dần (hoà theo tên) tới khi tỷ lệ cộng dồn ≥ ngưỡng %.

Yêu cầu

  • pareto(CAUSES, 80) ⇒ ba nguyên nhân đầu (81%).
hintsJson: Sắp giảm dần; cộng dồn; dừng khi cum ≥ ngưỡng × tổng.
So sánh bằng số nguyên (cum × 100 ≥ threshold × total) tránh sai số.

exercises.title: SPI 4 — the strongest incentive
exercises.problemHtml:
The strongest incentive for change is pain from previous projects: missed deadlines because requirements were bigger than expected, overtime from ambiguous requirements, wasted test effort, rework.

Each question is graded on its own; the explanation appears after you submit.
